sop_examples.title: Low Pump Pressure Response
sop_examples.condition: Pump outlet pressure has drifted below the 45 PSI minimum setpoint continuously for more than 30 seconds, indicating gradual supply degradation.

sop_examples.title: Sudden Pressure Collapse Response
sop_examples.condition: Pump outlet pressure drops from normal operating range to below 10 PSI within a single PLC scan cycle, indicating catastrophic instantaneous supply failure.

sop_examples.title: High Pump Pressure Alarm Response
sop_examples.condition: Pump outlet pressure exceeds the 120 PSI upper ceiling limit, creating risk of hose failure or seal damage.

sop_examples.title: Partial Nozzle Clog Warning
sop_examples.condition: Flow rate sensor reads 20 to 50 percent below target output while pump pressure remains within normal range, indicating partial obstruction in the nozzle tip.

sop_examples.title: Full Nozzle Blockage Emergency
sop_examples.condition: Flow rate sensor reads zero output while the pump is running and pressure is above setpoint, indicating complete nozzle obstruction with no flow reaching the part.

sop_examples.title: Adhesive Tank Low Level Alert
sop_examples.condition: Adhesive level sensor reads below 15 percent of tank capacity, requiring material replenishment before dispensing can resume.

sop_examples.title: Bead Width Below Specification
sop_examples.condition: Bead inspection camera reports applied bead width is consistently below the 4 mm lower control limit across three or more consecutive dispense cycles, indicating chronic under-dispensing.

sop_examples.title: Bead Width Above Specification
sop_examples.condition: Bead inspection camera reports applied bead width exceeds the 8 mm upper control limit, indicating over-dispensing or advanced nozzle wear.

sop_examples.title: Minor Adhesive Leak at Fitting
sop_examples.condition: Leak detection sensor at the hose coupling registers slow-drip accumulation below 50 mL total, indicating a weeping seal or loosened fitting connection.

sop_examples.title: Major Adhesive Hose Rupture Response
sop_examples.condition: Leak detection sensor exceeds the 500 mL emergency accumulation threshold or simultaneous hose-pressure drop and high-volume leak signal are active, indicating catastrophic hose or fitting rupture.

sop_examples.title: Pump Motor Electrical Fault Response
sop_examples.condition: Pump motor current sensor reads above the 15 A overload threshold or the motor controller fault code is active, indicating electrical overcurrent or drive failure.

sop_examples.title: Bead Inspection Camera Fault Recovery
sop_examples.condition: Bead inspection camera returns a null frame or loses signal for five or more consecutive dispense cycles, rendering in-process bead verification unavailable.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Nozzle Purge and Cleaning
sop_examples.condition: Scheduled 4-hour nozzle purge interval has elapsed or operator has requested a routine adhesive residue removal cycle to maintain tip cleanliness.

sop_examples.title: In-Line Adhesive Filter Replacement
sop_examples.condition: Filter differential pressure across the in-line adhesive strainer exceeds 8 PSI or the 200-hour service interval has been reached, requiring filter element replacement.

sop_examples.title: Pump Drive Gear Lubrication
sop_examples.condition: The 500-hour lubrication service interval for the pump drive gear assembly has been reached, requiring grease application to prevent mechanical wear.

sop_examples.title: Adhesive Tank Material Refill
sop_examples.condition: Shift supervisor has authorized adhesive material replenishment with a fresh cartridge staged at the machine and the robot holding production pending material availability.

sop_examples.title: Bead Width Inspection System Calibration
sop_examples.condition: Quality engineer requests calibration verification or bead width sensor readings diverge more than 0.5 mm from manual reference measurements on physical parts.

sop_examples.title: Adhesive Supply Hose Replacement
sop_examples.condition: Adhesive supply hose has exceeded its 1000-hour service life or shows visible cracking, swelling, or has required two or more leak interventions within a single shift.

sop_examples.title: Lockout-Tagout for Maintenance Access
sop_examples.condition: Maintenance technician requires physical access to dispenser internals, requiring full energy isolation and lockout-tagout before any work begins.

sop_examples.title: Fire or Smoke Emergency Stop
sop_examples.condition: Smoke or visible flame is detected at or near the adhesive dispenser unit, requiring immediate power isolation and emergency personnel notification.

sop_examples.title: Daily Startup Sequence
sop_examples.condition: Beginning-of-shift startup is required to bring the adhesive dispenser from cold standby to full production-ready operating status.

sop_examples.title: End-of-Shift Shutdown and Purge
sop_examples.condition: End-of-production-shift requires controlled adhesive purge, pump shutdown, and system de-pressurization before personnel leave the area.

sop_examples.title: Charging Voltage Below Setpoint Warning
sop_examples.condition: The charging voltage sensor reads between 21.0 V and 23.4 V during an active AGV docking cycle, triggering a low-voltage warning alarm while the unit continues to supply reduced power.

sop_examples.title: Charging Voltage Sudden Collapse Emergency
sop_examples.condition: The charging voltage sensor drops abruptly below 18.0 V in fewer than five seconds during an active docking cycle, indicating a sudden collapse rather than a gradual low-voltage drift, requiring immediate dock shutdown.

sop_examples.title: Charging Voltage Overvoltage Condition
sop_examples.condition: The charging voltage sensor reads above 29.5 V, exceeding the maximum allowable ceiling and triggering an overvoltage protection alarm that risks damage to the AGV battery management system.

sop_examples.title: Overcurrent During AGV Charging
sop_examples.condition: The charging current sensor reads above 85 A during an active charge cycle, exceeding the rated 80 A maximum and triggering the overcurrent alarm on the dock control panel.

sop_examples.title: Docking Contact Misalignment Fault
sop_examples.condition: The contact alignment sensor detects that the AGV charging contacts are offset beyond 3 mm from the dock receiver plate centerline, preventing a valid electrical connection from being established.

sop_examples.title: AGV Docking Approach Speed Degraded
sop_examples.condition: The AGV speed sensor registers a docking approach velocity below 0.05 m/s but above zero, indicating the vehicle is still in motion but moving far too slowly to complete a normal docking cycle within the timeout window.

sop_examples.title: AGV Fully Stopped Before Dock Contact
sop_examples.condition: The AGV speed sensor reads exactly zero and the dock presence sensor confirms the vehicle is within 200 mm of the dock receiver plate but has made no electrical contact, indicating a complete stall before connection is established.

sop_examples.title: Dock Proximity Sensor Hardware Failure
sop_examples.condition: The dock proximity sensor returns a fault code or a persistent no-signal state during normal operating conditions when AGV presence is known, indicating sensor hardware failure rather than a genuine absence of vehicle.

sop_examples.title: Electrical Arc Detected at Charging Contacts
sop_examples.condition: The arc detection sensor triggers a hard arc-fault alarm during AGV docking, indicating an uncontrolled high-energy electrical discharge between the vehicle contacts and the dock receiver plate requiring immediate dock de-energization.

sop_examples.title: Charging Unit Over-Temperature Fault
sop_examples.condition: The dock temperature sensor reads above 75 degrees C inside the charging unit enclosure, triggering the thermal protection alarm and requiring immediate cessation of charging operations to prevent component damage.

sop_examples.title: Minor Visible Spark at Dock During Connection
sop_examples.condition: An operator observes a brief, isolated visible spark at the charging contact point during initial AGV connection but the arc detection sensor reads below the alarm threshold, requiring logging and monitoring without immediate shutdown.

sop_examples.title: Worn Charging Contact Pad Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The contact wear sensor reading indicates the contact pads have reached or fallen below the minimum allowable thickness of 2 mm, requiring pad replacement before the next AGV charge cycle.

sop_examples.title: Dock Guide Rail and Actuator Lubrication
sop_examples.condition: Scheduled lubrication interval of 500 operating hours has been reached, or a technician detects audible friction or increased resistance from dock guide rails during AGV approach, requiring lubrication of rail and actuator surfaces.

sop_examples.title: Dock Proximity Sensor Calibration
sop_examples.condition: Scheduled 90-day calibration interval has been reached, or the dock proximity sensor shows a consistent position offset against known AGV reference positions, requiring recalibration to restore accurate vehicle detection range.

sop_examples.title: Charging Unit Cooling Filter Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The filter differential pressure sensor reads above 250 Pa, indicating the cooling and ventilation filter is clogged and requires replacement to restore adequate airflow through the charging unit enclosure.

sop_examples.title: Routine Charging Contact Surface Cleaning
sop_examples.condition: Scheduled weekly cleaning interval has been reached or visual inspection identifies minor oxide film or particulate contamination on the charging contact pad surfaces that is within acceptable cleaning limits and has not triggered any alarm.

sop_examples.title: AGV Charging Dock Lockout-Tagout Procedure
sop_examples.condition: Any maintenance or repair task on internal dock components requires full de-energization under a documented LOTO before a technician may physically access the charging unit enclosure or receiver plate assembly.

sop_examples.title: Emergency Stop and Station Isolation
sop_examples.condition: A fire, visible cable melt, smoke, or other imminent personnel safety hazard is observed at or adjacent to the AGV charging station, requiring immediate total dock shutdown and area isolation without waiting for a standard procedure sequence.

sop_examples.title: Shift Startup Procedure for AGV Charging Dock
sop_examples.condition: Beginning of a production shift or return from planned downtime requires verification of dock sensor readings and output voltage before AGV charging operations are authorized to resume.

sop_examples.title: Planned End-of-Shift Shutdown Procedure
sop_examples.condition: End of a production shift or entry into a planned maintenance window requires a controlled power-down sequence after all AGVs have cleared the dock, to ensure safe handover to the next crew or maintenance team.

sop_examples.title: Daily Visual and Sensor Readiness Inspection
sop_examples.condition: Beginning of each production day requires a systematic multi-sensor check of the AGV charging dock to confirm all sensors are within nominal range and no physical defects are present before the first AGV is dispatched.

sop_examples.title: Charging Contact Pad Wear Measurement
sop_examples.condition: Scheduled bi-weekly wear measurement interval has been reached or a supervisor requests a thickness check; the sensor reading indicates pads are worn but still above the 2 mm replacement minimum, requiring documentation without replacement action.

sop_examples.title: Gradual System Pressure Drop Below Setpoint
sop_examples.condition: System pressure sensor reads below the 90 PSI minimum setpoint for more than 60 consecutive seconds with no corresponding production load increase, indicating a slow ongoing loss event.

sop_examples.title: Sudden Catastrophic Pressure Collapse
sop_examples.condition: System pressure drops more than 20 PSI within 10 seconds, indicating a catastrophic loss event such as a burst distribution line, major valve failure, or large-area rupture.

sop_examples.title: System Pressure Exceeds Maximum Ceiling
sop_examples.condition: System pressure sensor reads above the 125 PSI maximum ceiling setpoint, triggering the high-pressure alarm while the compressor remains loaded and running without automatic unloading.

sop_examples.title: Discharge Temperature High Warning
sop_examples.condition: Discharge temperature sensor reads between 195 F and 210 F, triggering the amber warning-level alarm without initiating automatic compressor shutdown.

sop_examples.title: Discharge Temperature Emergency Shutdown
sop_examples.condition: Discharge temperature sensor reads above 210 F, causing the compressor control system to execute an automatic protective shutdown on a high-temperature fault.

sop_examples.title: Minor Air Leak at Receiver Tank Fittings
sop_examples.condition: Audible hiss or positive soap-bubble test at a receiver tank port or fitting, with system pressure loss less than 2 PSI per minute and no visible structural damage to the tank body.

sop_examples.title: Major Receiver Tank Rupture or Blowout
sop_examples.condition: Visible structural crack, loud percussive report, or catastrophic air release from the receiver tank body causes system pressure to drop to near-zero within 30 seconds.

sop_examples.title: Compressor Oil Level Low Alarm
sop_examples.condition: Oil level sensor reads below the minimum mark on the sight glass, triggering the low-oil alarm while the compressor remains operational and no temperature fault is present.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Compressor Oil Change
sop_examples.condition: Compressor has accumulated 2000 operating hours or oil analysis results indicate viscosity degradation or elevated metallic contamination requiring a full drain-and-fill.

sop_examples.title: Intake Air Filter Element Replacement
sop_examples.condition: Differential pressure sensor across the intake filter exceeds 4 inches W.C., or 500 operating hours have elapsed since the last filter element replacement.

sop_examples.title: Oil-Air Separator Element Replacement
sop_examples.condition: Separator differential pressure sensor reads above 10 PSI, indicating a clogged separator element that must be replaced to prevent oil carry-over into the distribution system.

sop_examples.title: Drive Belt Inspection and Replacement
sop_examples.condition: Scheduled 1000-hour belt inspection interval is reached, or audible squealing or visible cracking and glazing is observed on the compressor drive belt during rounds.

sop_examples.title: Refrigerant Dryer Coalescing Filter Replacement
sop_examples.condition: Dryer coalescing filter differential pressure indicator reads above 15 PSI, or 1000 operating hours have elapsed since the last dryer filter element replacement.

sop_examples.title: Motor and Fan Bearing Lubrication
sop_examples.condition: Lubrication interval of 2000 operating hours has been reached for the compressor motor and cooling fan bearing grease fittings per the preventive maintenance schedule.

sop_examples.title: Pressure Relief Valve Annual Functional Test
sop_examples.condition: Annual scheduled functional test of the receiver tank pressure relief valve is due, requiring verification that the valve lifts and reseats at its rated set pressure.

sop_examples.title: Pressure Switch Setpoint Calibration
sop_examples.condition: Scheduled 6-month calibration of the compressor cut-in and cut-out pressure switch setpoints is due, or observed cycling points deviate from engineering specifications by more than 2 PSI.

sop_examples.title: Compressor Lockout Tagout for Maintenance
sop_examples.condition: Any maintenance activity requiring physical access to compressor internals, electrical panels, or pressurized components mandates full energy isolation per plant LOTO procedure before work begins.

sop_examples.title: Compressor Oil Spill Response
sop_examples.condition: Oil is visible on the floor beneath the compressor unit or a drain pan overflow is detected, creating a slip hazard that requires immediate containment and cleanup.

sop_examples.title: Emergency Stop for Fire or Smoke Near Compressor
sop_examples.condition: Smoke, visible flame, or strong burning odor is detected in or immediately adjacent to the compressor room, requiring immediate energy isolation and fire response.

sop_examples.title: Standard Compressor Daily Startup Procedure
sop_examples.condition: Daily startup at the beginning of the production shift, or restart following a planned shutdown or completed maintenance window after all LOTO devices have been removed.

sop_examples.title: Standard Planned Compressor Shutdown
sop_examples.condition: End-of-shift or scheduled planned shutdown is required with no maintenance access needed, calling for a controlled unload-and-stop sequence that leaves the unit in a safe idle state.

sop_examples.title: Weekly Walk-Around Inspection and Logging
sop_examples.condition: Weekly scheduled inspection interval has been reached, requiring visual verification and sensor logging of all major compressor and dryer subsystems before the maintenance log is signed off.

sop_examples.title: Gradual Steam Pressure Below Setpoint
sop_examples.condition: Steam header pressure sensor reads below the normal operating setpoint of 90 PSI for more than 2 minutes without a corresponding increase in process load.

sop_examples.title: Rapid Steam Pressure Collapse
sop_examples.condition: Steam pressure sensor registers a drop of more than 20 PSI within 30 seconds, indicating a possible steam line breach or sudden catastrophic load event.

sop_examples.title: Steam Pressure High Warning
sop_examples.condition: Steam pressure sensor reads above the high-pressure warning threshold of 125 PSI but below the pressure relief setpoint of 150 PSI.

sop_examples.title: Pressure Relief Valve Active Discharge
sop_examples.condition: The pressure relief valve is actively venting steam to atmosphere, confirming that boiler pressure has exceeded the 150 PSI safety ceiling.

sop_examples.title: Boiler Drum Water Level Below Minimum
sop_examples.condition: Water level sensor in the boiler drum reads below the minimum safe operating level of 30% for more than 60 seconds during normal operation.

sop_examples.title: Sudden Rapid Water Level Collapse
sop_examples.condition: Water level sensor drops more than 25 percentage points within 60 seconds, indicating a probable tube failure, ruptured drum fitting, or blowdown valve stuck in the open position.

sop_examples.title: Boiler Drum Water Level Above Maximum
sop_examples.condition: Water level sensor reads above the maximum safe operating level of 85%, creating risk of water carryover and water hammer in steam distribution lines.

sop_examples.title: Burner Flame Loss and Safety Lockout
sop_examples.condition: Flame sensor detects loss of burner flame and the burner control module locks out after two consecutive failed ignition attempts.

sop_examples.title: Flue Gas Temperature Excessive at Stack Outlet
sop_examples.condition: Flue gas temperature sensor at the boiler stack outlet reads above 450 degrees F, indicating fouled heat transfer surfaces or an excessively high firing rate.

sop_examples.title: Feedwater Pump Stopped or Insufficient Flow
sop_examples.condition: Feedwater pump run-status sensor indicates the primary pump has stopped or the feedwater flow sensor reads below the minimum threshold during normal boiler operation.

sop_examples.title: Small Continuous Water Leak at Fitting or Packing
sop_examples.condition: Floor leak sensor or visual inspection detects a small persistent drip or seep from a boiler fitting, valve packing, or threaded pipe joint with no accompanying pressure deviation.

sop_examples.title: Steam or Water Line Major Rupture
sop_examples.condition: A large uncontrolled water or steam release is detected simultaneously by the floor leak sensor and a rapid steam pressure drop, or a pipe, tube, or drum fitting failure with substantial uncontrolled flow is directly observed.

sop_examples.title: Water Softener Regeneration Required
sop_examples.condition: Water hardness sensor at the softener outlet reads above the maximum allowable hardness setpoint or the scheduled regeneration interval of 72 hours has elapsed.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Bottom Blowdown for Sediment Removal
sop_examples.condition: Daily maintenance schedule requires bottom blowdown to purge sediment and scale from the boiler drum, or the TDS sensor reads above 3500 ppm.

sop_examples.title: Water Gauge Glass Inspection and Cleaning
sop_examples.condition: Weekly maintenance schedule requires inspection and cleaning of the boiler water gauge glass, or the glass is visibly cloudy, stained, or otherwise obscured.

sop_examples.title: Burner Nozzle Scheduled Replacement
sop_examples.condition: Accumulated operating hours on the burner nozzle have reached the 2000-hour replacement interval or the combustion efficiency sensor shows CO emissions above 50 ppm.

sop_examples.title: Pressure Safety Relief Valve Monthly Lift Test
sop_examples.condition: Monthly preventive maintenance schedule requires a manual lift test of the pressure safety relief valve to verify it opens freely and reseats without leaking.

sop_examples.title: Boiler Full Lockout Tagout Isolation
sop_examples.condition: A maintenance work order requires complete isolation and de-energization of the boiler system before any internal inspection, cleaning, or repair is performed.

sop_examples.title: Steam Burn or Scalding Injury Response
sop_examples.condition: A worker sustains a burn or scalding injury from a steam release or hot condensate contact in the boiler room.

sop_examples.title: Carbon Monoxide Alarm Activation in Boiler Room
sop_examples.condition: Carbon monoxide detector in the boiler room activates with a reading at or above 35 ppm, indicating incomplete combustion or flue gas recirculation into the occupied space.

sop_examples.title: Boiler Cold Start from De-Pressurized State
sop_examples.condition: Boiler has been fully de-pressurized and cooled to ambient temperature following a planned outage and must be returned to normal operating pressure and temperature.

sop_examples.title: Controlled Planned Boiler Shutdown
sop_examples.condition: A scheduled maintenance window, end-of-production period, or planned outage requires controlled reduction of boiler pressure and safe de-energization of all systems.

sop_examples.title: Capping Machine Daily Startup
sop_examples.condition: Machine is in powered-off state at the start of a production shift and the surrounding area has been verified clear of personnel.

sop_examples.title: Capping Machine Daily Shutdown
sop_examples.condition: End-of-shift shutdown is required after all bottles have cleared the capping station and no further production is scheduled.

sop_examples.title: Cap Chute Jam Clearance
sop_examples.condition: The cap chute jam sensor has triggered and cap flow to the torque head has stopped with caps visibly stacked or bridged inside the chute.

sop_examples.title: Torque Head Over-Torque Fault Response
sop_examples.condition: The torque monitoring sensor reads ABOVE the maximum torque setpoint for more than two consecutive capping cycles, triggering a persistent overtorque alarm.

sop_examples.title: Torque Head Chronic Under-Torque Fault Response
sop_examples.condition: The torque monitoring sensor reads persistently BELOW the minimum setpoint across multiple consecutive cycles, indicating insufficient capping force rather than any single-cycle spike.

sop_examples.title: Mid-Cycle Torque Sudden Collapse Response
sop_examples.condition: The torque sensor detects an abrupt single-cycle drop to near-zero during capping engagement — not a chronic low-torque pattern — indicating a stripped clutch, slipped spindle, or mechanical failure in one instant.

sop_examples.title: Reject Gate Actuation Failure
sop_examples.condition: The reject gate actuator has failed to physically extend or retract on command when a non-conforming bottle is detected, confirmed by the gate position sensor showing an incorrect mechanical state.

sop_examples.title: Cap Hopper Low Level Warning Response
sop_examples.condition: The cap hopper level sensor reads below the low-level warning threshold but has NOT yet triggered the empty alarm; cap flow is still active and production can continue briefly while caps are replenished.

sop_examples.title: Cap Hopper Empty Alarm Response
sop_examples.condition: The cap hopper level sensor has triggered the empty alarm and cap flow has completely stopped, halting all capping activity until the hopper is reloaded and flow is confirmed.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Torque Head and Drive Chain Lubrication
sop_examples.condition: The scheduled lubrication interval has been reached per the preventive maintenance calendar (every 500 operating hours or weekly, whichever comes first).

sop_examples.title: Drive Belt Scheduled Replacement
sop_examples.condition: Weekly inspection reveals cracks, fraying, or measured elongation in the drive belt beyond the wear limit documented on the inspection card.

sop_examples.title: Torque Head Scheduled Calibration
sop_examples.condition: The weekly torque calibration task is due on the PM schedule, or quality inspection data shows torque readings drifting more than five percent from verified reference values.

sop_examples.title: Emergency Stop Activation Response
sop_examples.condition: The red E-stop button has been pressed by any personnel due to an imminent safety hazard and the machine has halted mid-cycle with the estop indicator lit.

sop_examples.title: Lockout Tagout Procedure for Maintenance Access
sop_examples.condition: Planned maintenance work requiring physical access to machine internals has been scheduled and the capping machine must be fully de-energized and locked out before work begins.

sop_examples.title: Cap Chute Routine Cleaning
sop_examples.condition: Scheduled daily cleaning of the cap chute interior is due, or cap debris and residue are visibly present inside the chute affecting cap alignment before reaching the torque head.

sop_examples.title: Reject Sensor Misalignment Warning Response
sop_examples.condition: The reject lane vision sensor has reported a WARNING-level alignment error with degraded signal strength but the gate is still actuating and no confirmed missed rejects have been detected yet.

sop_examples.title: Bottle Infeed Conveyor Low Speed Warning
sop_examples.condition: The conveyor speed sensor reads below the minimum production setpoint but the infeed belt is still moving and bottles are still feeding, generating a low-speed warning rather than a stop alarm.

sop_examples.title: Bottle Infeed Conveyor Fully Stopped Alarm
sop_examples.condition: The conveyor speed sensor reads zero and the motor overload indicator is active, indicating the infeed conveyor belt has completely stopped rather than merely slowed, requiring a motor fault reset.

sop_examples.title: Drive Inverter Electrical Fault Response
sop_examples.condition: The drive inverter fault indicator lamp is illuminated and the inverter fault code sensor is active, indicating a drive-side electrical fault that has caused the machine to stop and requires maintenance intervention before reset.

sop_examples.title: Cap Orientation Fault Quality Inspection Response
sop_examples.condition: The cap orientation sensor has detected caps arriving at the torque head in an inverted or skewed position, causing quality reject counts to exceed the acceptable threshold.

sop_examples.title: Lubricant or Fluid Spill Response
sop_examples.condition: A lubricant or hydraulic fluid spill has been identified on the floor area surrounding the capping machine base, creating an active slip hazard that must be contained before production resumes.

sop_examples.title: Torque Head Pneumatic Filter Scheduled Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The scheduled pneumatic filter replacement interval has been reached per the PM log (every 1,000 operating hours), or the filter differential pressure sensor reads above the clog threshold indicating restriction in the torque head air supply.

sop_examples.title: Glue Temperature Below Setpoint
sop_examples.condition: The hot-melt glue temperature sensor reads below the minimum operating setpoint, causing the adhesive to become viscous and poorly flowable during a production run.
steps: notify shift_supervisor if temperature has not recovered to setpoint

sop_examples.title: Glue Temperature Above Upper Limit
sop_examples.condition: The hot-melt glue temperature sensor reads above the maximum allowable limit, causing adhesive scorching and runny bead formation on carton flaps.

sop_examples.title: Sudden Glue Temperature Collapse Mid-Run
sop_examples.condition: The hot-melt glue temperature drops more than 40 degrees Celsius within 60 seconds during an active production run, indicating a heater element failure or sudden power interruption.

sop_examples.title: Glue Tank Level Low Warning
sop_examples.condition: The glue tank level sensor triggers the yellow warning threshold at approximately 25 percent capacity, signaling that a refill is needed soon but the machine continues running normally.

sop_examples.title: Glue Tank Empty Critical Alarm
sop_examples.condition: The glue tank level sensor hits the red critical threshold and the machine halts dispensing entirely, triggering a red alarm and full production stoppage.

sop_examples.title: Case Blank Jam at Infeed Conveyor
sop_examples.condition: A case blank becomes misaligned or folded at the infeed conveyor or erector entry point, triggering the infeed jam sensor and stopping the blank feed mechanism.

sop_examples.title: Packed Case Jam at Discharge Conveyor
sop_examples.condition: A fully packed and sealed case becomes misaligned or wedged on the discharge conveyor downstream of the glue station, blocking subsequent cases and triggering the discharge jam sensor.

sop_examples.title: Pusher Servo Overload Fault
sop_examples.condition: The pusher servo drive detects an overcurrent or mechanical overload and faults out, stopping the pusher arm and halting case loading into the former.

sop_examples.title: Former Belt Slipping and Misaligned
sop_examples.condition: The former belt is drifting laterally off its center guide and occasionally skipping, causing intermittent misfolded case bottoms, but the belt continues to move at reduced effectiveness.

sop_examples.title: Former Belt Fully Stopped or Broken
sop_examples.condition: The former belt has completely stopped moving or has physically broken, causing total cessation of case erection and triggering the former belt fault sensor.

sop_examples.title: VFD Drive Electrical Fault Alarm
sop_examples.condition: The variable-frequency drive controlling the main conveyor motor trips and displays a fault code, stopping the conveyor without any mechanical jam present.

sop_examples.title: Minor Glue Drip at Nozzle Head
sop_examples.condition: A slow, continuous glue drip or seep is detected at the nozzle head fitting or manifold, forming a small puddle on the deck plate without spray or pressure loss.

sop_examples.title: Major Hot Melt Hose Rupture
sop_examples.condition: A hot-melt glue hose or high-pressure fitting fails catastrophically, releasing a large volume of pressurized hot adhesive onto the floor and surrounding equipment.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Glue Nozzle Cleaning
sop_examples.condition: Preventive maintenance schedule requires cleaning of the glue nozzle orifice to remove charred adhesive buildup that restricts bead consistency.

sop_examples.title: Conveyor Chain and Rail Lubrication
sop_examples.condition: Preventive maintenance schedule requires lubrication of conveyor chains and guide rails to prevent wear, noise, and premature failure.

sop_examples.title: Former Belt Scheduled Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The former belt has reached its scheduled end-of-life interval or shows visible cracking, splitting, or fraying that warrants a planned replacement during a scheduled maintenance window.

sop_examples.title: Hot Melt Glue Filter Replacement
sop_examples.condition: Preventive maintenance schedule requires replacement of the hot-melt glue filter element, or reduced glue flow is observed with a full tank indicating filter restriction.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Hot Melt Glue Tank Refill
sop_examples.condition: The glue tank level reads between 25 and 50 percent during a planned refill window before a production shift, with the machine still operational and no alarm active.

sop_examples.title: Case Position Encoder Recalibration
sop_examples.condition: After a maintenance rebuild or mechanical adjustment to the infeed drive, the case position encoder reads incorrectly, causing cases to phase out of sync with the pusher and former timing.

sop_examples.title: Packed Case Seal and Dimension Inspection
sop_examples.condition: Routine quality checkpoint requires sampling of finished cases from the discharge conveyor to verify glue seal integrity and dimensional compliance to specification.

sop_examples.title: Full Machine Lockout Tagout
sop_examples.condition: Maintenance work requiring entry into guarded areas or contact with mechanical or electrical components of the case packer requires full lockout and tagout of all energy sources.

sop_examples.title: Emergency Stop Activation and Area Clearance
sop_examples.condition: A safety hazard such as a fire, severe injury risk, or detected electrical short requires immediate emergency stop activation and evacuation of the machine area.

sop_examples.title: Refrigerant Low Pressure Sustained Alarm Response
sop_examples.condition: The suction pressure sensor reads below the 45 PSI minimum setpoint continuously for more than 5 minutes, generating a yellow alarm on the chiller HMI while the compressor remains running.

sop_examples.title: Sudden Refrigerant Pressure Collapse Emergency Response
sop_examples.condition: The suction pressure sensor records a drop exceeding 20 PSI within 60 seconds, indicating rapid system depressurization rather than a slow drift.

sop_examples.title: Discharge Refrigerant Pressure Over-Limit Response
sop_examples.condition: The discharge pressure sensor reads above the 400 PSI ceiling and triggers a red high-pressure alarm, with the system still running but at risk of safety relief valve actuation.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Outlet Temperature High Warning Response
sop_examples.condition: The coolant outlet temperature sensor reads above the 16 degrees C upper setpoint but below the 20 degrees C critical ceiling, generating a sustained yellow warning on the HMI while the chiller continues to run.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Outlet Temperature Critical Interlock Response
sop_examples.condition: The coolant outlet temperature sensor reads above the 20 degrees C critical ceiling, triggering a red emergency alarm and an automatic process interlock that halts downstream production equipment.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Outlet Temperature Below Setpoint Response
sop_examples.condition: The coolant outlet temperature sensor reads below the 6 degrees C lower setpoint, indicating over-cooling or a failed-open expansion valve causing excessive refrigeration.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Pump Flow Rate Low Warning Response
sop_examples.condition: The coolant flow sensor reads below 80 percent of the 120 GPM setpoint but above zero GPM for more than 2 minutes, generating a sustained low-flow warning on the HMI while the pump motor remains energized.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Pump Complete No-Flow Emergency Response
sop_examples.condition: The coolant flow sensor reads zero GPM continuously for more than 10 seconds, indicating the circulating pump has stopped entirely and compressor cooling is lost.

sop_examples.title: Condenser Fan Motor Electrical Fault Response
sop_examples.condition: The condenser fan motor overload relay has tripped and the fan status indicator on the panel shows a fault code, halting condenser heat rejection while the compressor continues to run.

sop_examples.title: Compressor Motor Overload Fault Response
sop_examples.condition: The compressor motor overload relay has tripped and the chiller has auto-shut on a compressor fault alarm, with the pump and condenser fans still able to run.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Filter Scheduled Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The filter differential pressure sensor reads above 15 PSI or the 500-hour scheduled change interval has elapsed, indicating the filter element is loaded and must be replaced.

sop_examples.title: Condenser Coil Scheduled Cleaning
sop_examples.condition: The condenser approach temperature difference exceeds 5 degrees C above the established baseline, indicating fouled fin surfaces that reduce heat rejection capacity.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Pump Bearing Scheduled Lubrication
sop_examples.condition: The 1000-hour pump bearing lubrication interval has elapsed or the pump bearing temperature sensor reads above 75 degrees C during operation.

sop_examples.title: Refrigerant Level and Leak Weekly Inspection
sop_examples.condition: The scheduled weekly refrigerant inspection interval is due, or the chiller room refrigerant gas detector has triggered a low-level advisory alert.

sop_examples.title: Chiller Temperature Sensor Quarterly Calibration
sop_examples.condition: The quarterly calibration interval has elapsed or a spot check reveals any chiller temperature sensor reading more than 1 degree C from a certified reference thermometer.

sop_examples.title: Pump Drive Belt Scheduled Replacement
sop_examples.condition: A visual inspection reveals cracking, glazing, or more than 5 mm of deflection on the pump drive belt, or the 2000-hour replacement interval has elapsed.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Y-Strainer Basket Cleaning
sop_examples.condition: The strainer differential pressure sensor reads above 8 PSI, indicating the Y-strainer basket is fouled and restricting pump suction flow.

sop_examples.title: Chiller Lockout Tagout for Maintenance Access
sop_examples.condition: Any scheduled or corrective maintenance task requires physical access to the chiller unit interior, creating an obligation to isolate all electrical and mechanical energy sources before work begins.

sop_examples.title: Refrigerant Release and Spill Emergency Response
sop_examples.condition: The chiller room refrigerant gas detector triggers a high-concentration alarm or visible frost and ice accumulation is observed at a fitting, joint, or hose connection on the refrigerant loop.

sop_examples.title: Chiller Emergency Stop for Immediate Safety Threat
sop_examples.condition: An immediate safety threat such as smoke, burning electrical odor, loud mechanical impact noise, or an operator distress call requires instant manual shutdown of the chiller independent of any fault alarm.

sop_examples.title: Chiller Startup After De-Energization
sop_examples.condition: The chiller has been fully de-energized for maintenance or an extended shutdown and must be returned to normal cooling service following clearance from maintenance personnel.

sop_examples.title: Chiller Planned Controlled Shutdown Procedure
sop_examples.condition: A planned maintenance window or end-of-production period requires the chiller to be taken offline in the correct controlled sequence to prevent thermal shock and compressor damage.

sop_examples.title: Daily CMM Startup Sequence
sop_examples.condition: The CMM has been fully powered off overnight and must be initialized for the incoming production shift.

sop_examples.title: End-of-Shift CMM Shutdown Sequence
sop_examples.condition: The production shift has ended and the CMM must be safely parked, probe stowed, and controller powered down.

sop_examples.title: Pre-Measurement Thermal Stabilization
sop_examples.condition: The CMM has been powered on but ambient temperature in the measurement room has not yet stabilized to the required 20 degrees C before dimensional inspection may begin.

sop_examples.title: Air Bearing Pressure Below Minimum Threshold
sop_examples.condition: Air supply pressure to the CMM air bearings has drifted gradually below the 5.5 bar minimum setpoint, triggering a sustained low-pressure warning alarm.

sop_examples.title: Sudden Air Bearing Pressure Collapse
sop_examples.condition: Air bearing supply pressure has collapsed more than 1.5 bar within ten seconds, indicating a supply line rupture or valve failure requiring immediate machine halt.

sop_examples.title: Air Bearing Pressure Exceeds Upper Limit
sop_examples.condition: Air bearing supply pressure has climbed above the 6.5 bar ceiling, risking permanent damage to the precision air bearing surfaces.

sop_examples.title: Probe Contact Force Elevated Warning
sop_examples.condition: Probe contact force sensor reads between 0.15 N and 0.25 N, above the nominal 0.10 N but below the fault threshold, indicating possible tip contamination or probe stiffness.

sop_examples.title: Probe Contact Force Critical Fault
sop_examples.condition: Probe contact force sensor has exceeded the 0.25 N fault threshold, causing the CMM controller to freeze all axis motion and raise a hard fault alarm.

sop_examples.title: Measurement Area Temperature Below Setpoint
sop_examples.condition: Measurement room temperature has fallen below 19 degrees C, outside the plus-or-minus 1 degree C ISO tolerance band, causing the CMM to automatically suspend active measurements.

sop_examples.title: Measurement Area Temperature Rapid Rise Above Ceiling
sop_examples.condition: Measurement room temperature has risen above 22 degrees C within a fifteen-minute window, indicating HVAC failure or external heat intrusion requiring immediate machine shutdown.

sop_examples.title: Chipped Stylus Ball Detected on Visual Inspection
sop_examples.condition: Visual inspection has identified a chip or surface crack on the ruby stylus ball, making dimensional readings unreliable while the probe motion mechanism remains functional.

sop_examples.title: Bent Stylus Shaft Detected by Qualification Failure
sop_examples.condition: The automated probe qualification routine against the reference sphere has exceeded the 2 micrometer tolerance, indicating the stylus shaft is physically deformed and no longer coaxial.

sop_examples.title: Lockout-Tagout for Scheduled CMM Maintenance
sop_examples.condition: Scheduled preventive maintenance requires all electrical and pneumatic energy sources on the CMM to be fully isolated and locked before any panel or cover is opened.

sop_examples.title: Minor Coolant Drip Near Granite Table Base
sop_examples.condition: A small coolant drip of less than 0.5 liters has been detected near the base of the granite table structure, with the table surface itself remaining uncontaminated.

sop_examples.title: Major Coolant Flood Contaminating Granite Table Surface
sop_examples.condition: Greater than 2 liters of coolant has pooled on or across the granite table surface, contaminating the measurement datum and creating an immediate slip hazard on the surrounding floor.

sop_examples.title: Emergency Stop Activated During Active Measurement Cycle
sop_examples.condition: The red E-stop button has been pressed while the CMM is executing a measurement cycle, leaving the probe axes halted mid-travel with a workpiece still fixtured on the granite table.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Air Supply Filter Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The CMM air supply inline filter has reached its 500-hour replacement interval, or the filter differential pressure sensor reads above 0.3 bar.

sop_examples.title: Probe Stylus Calibration with Reference Sphere
sop_examples.condition: A new stylus tip has been installed, or the four-hour calibration interval has elapsed, requiring re-qualification of the probe tip position against the precision reference sphere.

sop_examples.title: Routine Granite Table Surface Cleaning
sop_examples.condition: End-of-shift or between-batch cleaning of the granite surface is required to remove metal chips, coolant residue, and dust that could affect part seating accuracy.

sop_examples.title: Linear Scale Encoder Cleaning Procedure
sop_examples.condition: Scheduled 1000-hour maintenance or an axis repeatability test has detected intermittent encoder read errors requiring cleaning of the linear glass scale and read head.

sop_examples.title: Controller Cabinet Cooling Filter Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The controller cabinet cooling filter has reached its 250-hour replacement interval, or the cabinet internal temperature sensor reads above 45 degrees C.

sop_examples.title: Reference Artifact Dimensional Verification
sop_examples.condition: Daily pre-production verification of the calibration artifact is required on the granite table to confirm CMM volumetric accuracy is within specification before any production parts are inspected.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Pressure Below Minimum Setpoint
sop_examples.condition: The coolant pressure sensor reads below 2.0 bar for more than 30 seconds during a cutting cycle, triggering a P-LOW alarm while the spindle and axes continue operating.
steps: notify maintenance_tech if pressure remains below 2.0 bar

sop_examples.title: Sudden Coolant Pressure Collapse to Zero
sop_examples.condition: Coolant pressure drops from the normal operating range to zero bar within 5 seconds during a cut, indicating a ruptured line or pump seizure, and the controller halts all motion on a P-FAULT alarm.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Pressure Above Maximum Ceiling
sop_examples.condition: The coolant pressure sensor reads above 6.5 bar, the system maximum, triggering a P-HIGH alarm that risks rupturing nozzle seals and supply fittings if left unaddressed.
steps: notify maintenance_tech if pressure remains above 6.5 bar

sop_examples.title: Spindle Load at Warning Threshold
sop_examples.condition: The spindle load monitor reads between 75% and 99% of rated capacity, illuminating a steady LOAD-WARN indicator while the spindle continues rotating at the programmed speed without faulting.
steps: notify operator_lead if load remains above 75%

sop_examples.title: Spindle Overload Fault and Full Stop
sop_examples.condition: Spindle load exceeds 100% of rated capacity and the controller trips an OVL-FAULT alarm, cutting power to the spindle motor and halting all axis motion with the workpiece clamped in the chuck.

sop_examples.title: Chuck Hydraulic Grip Pressure Loss
sop_examples.condition: The hydraulic chuck pressure sensor reads below 35 bar, the minimum safe clamping threshold, causing a GRIP-LOW alarm that locks out spindle start to prevent workpiece ejection.
steps: notify maintenance_tech if pressure remains below 35 bar

sop_examples.title: Turret Indexing Jam Between Tool Stations
sop_examples.condition: The turret fails to complete rotation to the commanded tool station within the controller timeout window, triggering a TURR-JAM alarm and halting all axis motion.
steps: notify maintenance_tech if turret does not index to station

sop_examples.title: Bar Feeder Stock Advance Jam
sop_examples.condition: The bar feeder fails to advance the stock bar to the collet stop position within the programmed feed time, triggering a FEED-JAM alarm on the bar feeder display and halting the cycle.

sop_examples.title: Axis Position Encoder Fault
sop_examples.condition: The CNC controller raises an ENCODER-FAULT alarm for the X or Z axis, indicating a lost or erratic position signal that prevents safe axis movement until the fault is cleared.

sop_examples.title: Minor Coolant Drip at Chip Conveyor Seal
sop_examples.condition: A slow coolant drip of less than 0.5 liters per minute is observed at the chip conveyor drain seal or fitting, posing a floor slip hazard but not requiring machine stoppage.

sop_examples.title: Major Coolant Line Rupture
sop_examples.condition: Coolant is flowing uncontrolled at more than 2 liters per minute from a ruptured line or blown fitting, spreading across the floor and creating an immediate slip and electrical hazard.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Filter Media Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The coolant filter differential pressure indicator reaches the red zone or the 250 operating-hour scheduled replacement interval has elapsed, reducing coolant flow and filtration efficiency.

sop_examples.title: Machine Way and Ball Screw Lubrication
sop_examples.condition: The centralized lubrication system low-oil indicator illuminates, or the daily lubrication log shows the manual way-oiling interval has elapsed, requiring the reservoir to be topped up and the lube pump primed.

sop_examples.title: Spindle Drive Belt Inspection and Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The 1000-hour spindle belt inspection interval is due, or audible squealing or measurable belt slippage is detected during spindle acceleration to programmed speed.

sop_examples.title: Chip Conveyor and Collection Bin Cleanout
sop_examples.condition: The BIN-FULL sensor activates when the chip collection bin reaches 80% capacity, or visible chip buildup is impeding conveyor belt movement and risking a jam.

sop_examples.title: Tool Length Offset Calibration After Insert Change
sop_examples.condition: A new cutting insert or toolholder has been mounted in a turret station and the corresponding tool offset register must be updated before resuming production to maintain dimensional accuracy.

sop_examples.title: Full Lockout-Tagout for Maintenance Zone Entry
sop_examples.condition: Planned maintenance requiring physical entry into the machine work zone or access to guarded mechanical areas mandates isolation of all electrical and hydraulic energy sources before work begins.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Spill Cleanup on Floor
sop_examples.condition: A static coolant puddle of less than 5 liters is found on the floor around the lathe base with no active source of flow, posing a slip hazard that must be absorbed and disposed of as chemical waste.

sop_examples.title: Fire or Smoke Emergency Stop and Evacuation
sop_examples.condition: Smoke, visible flame, or a fire alarm activation is detected in or adjacent to the CNC lathe cell, requiring immediate power isolation, alarm pull, and area evacuation.

sop_examples.title: Daily Machine Startup Sequence
sop_examples.condition: The CNC lathe has been powered down overnight or during a shift break and must be brought to full production-ready status, including axis homing and coolant system priming.

sop_examples.title: End-of-Shift Machine Shutdown Sequence
sop_examples.condition: The production shift is ending and the CNC lathe must be safely shut down, with the cutting cycle stopped, coolant pump secured, chip conveyor halted, and main power removed.

sop_examples.title: Part Dimension Out-of-Tolerance Inspection and Offset Adjust
sop_examples.condition: In-process gauging or a first-article inspection reveals a turned diameter or faced length is outside the blueprint tolerance band, triggering a GAUGE-OOR alert and requiring a tool offset correction before the next part.

sop_examples.title: Spindle Overspeed Alarm Response
sop_examples.condition: CNC controller alarm panel indicates spindle RPM has exceeded the programmed maximum allowed ceiling.
steps: Press spindle_stop_button to halt spindle rotation immediately.
Walk to HMI_panel and read_sensor spindle_rpm_display to confirm the overspeed reading.
Press feed_hold_button to suspend all axis motion.
Read_sensor spindle_drive_alarm_code to capture the fault code.
Notify maintenance_technician of spindle overspeed alarm with current RPM value and fault code.
Wait 30 seconds for spindle to decelerate fully.
Pick fault_log_clipboard and place at supervisor_station for review.

sop_examples.title: Spindle Underspeed During Active Cut
sop_examples.condition: Spindle RPM drifts gradually below the programmed setpoint while an active cutting pass is in progress.
steps: Read_sensor spindle_rpm_sensor to confirm RPM is below the programmed setpoint.
Press feed_hold_button to pause axis feed without terminating the program.
Notify CNC_operator of gradual underspeed condition and current RPM value.
Read_sensor spindle_load_meter to check for belt slip or drive overload signature.
Wait 15 seconds for spindle drive to stabilize.
Read_sensor spindle_rpm_sensor again to determine if RPM self-recovers to setpoint.
If RPM remains below setpoint, press spindle_stop_button and notify maintenance_technician.

sop_examples.title: Sudden Spindle Stall Mid-Cut
sop_examples.condition: Spindle comes to a sudden and complete stop with no gradual deceleration while a cutting tool is engaged in the workpiece.
steps: Press estop_button immediately to halt all machine motion and power to drives.
Read_sensor spindle_drive_fault_display to capture the stall fault code.
Notify maintenance_technician of sudden spindle stall event with fault code and tool-in-cut status.
Press coolant_off_button to stop coolant flow and prevent flooding the engaged workpiece.
Read_sensor spindle_motor_temp_sensor to check for thermal overload condition.
Wait 60 seconds before any restart attempt to allow drive capacitors to discharge.
Pick fault_log_clipboard and place at maintenance_station for technician review.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Pressure Below Minimum Setpoint
sop_examples.condition: Coolant pressure sensor reads below the minimum threshold setpoint for more than five continuous seconds during machining.
steps: Read_sensor coolant_pressure_gauge to confirm the reading is below the minimum setpoint.
Press feed_hold_button to suspend axis motion while coolant delivery is insufficient.
Walk to coolant_pump_panel and read_sensor coolant_pump_status_light to verify pump state.
Read_sensor coolant_level_sensor to determine if low tank level is the root cause.
Notify maintenance_technician of low coolant pressure alarm with current gauge reading.
Wait 20 seconds for system pressure to stabilize after axis feed is held.
Press coolant_pump_reset_button if pump has tripped, then read_sensor coolant_pressure_gauge to confirm recovery.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Pressure Exceeds Upper Alarm Limit
sop_examples.condition: Coolant pressure gauge reading rises above the upper alarm limit, indicating a restriction or relief valve failure in the coolant circuit.
steps: Press coolant_off_button immediately to de-energize the coolant pump.
Read_sensor coolant_pressure_gauge to log the peak pressure value reached.
Walk to coolant_filter_housing and read_sensor filter_bypass_indicator to check for filter blockage causing back-pressure.
Notify maintenance_technician of high coolant pressure alarm with peak reading.
Wait 30 seconds for residual system pressure to bleed down.
Read_sensor coolant_pressure_gauge to confirm pressure has returned to normal range.
If filter_bypass_indicator is active, pick coolant_filter_element and place at inspection_bench for replacement.

sop_examples.title: Zero Coolant Flow While Pump Is Running
sop_examples.condition: Coolant flow sensor reads zero flow rate while the spindle is running and the coolant pump is commanded on.
steps: Read_sensor coolant_flow_sensor to confirm a zero flow rate reading.
Press spindle_stop_button immediately to halt cutting with no coolant present.
Notify CNC_operator that coolant delivery has completely failed and production is halted.
Walk to coolant_pump_panel and read_sensor coolant_pump_status_light to check pump state.
Read_sensor coolant_level_sensor to verify the tank has not run dry.
Notify maintenance_technician of total coolant flow failure for pump and line inspection.
Pick lockout_tag and place at coolant_pump_panel before any pump maintenance begins.

sop_examples.title: Axis Servo Drive Fault Response
sop_examples.condition: CNC controller reports an axis servo drive overcurrent or position-error fault, halting all coordinated axis motion.
steps: Read_sensor servo_fault_display to capture the fault code and the affected axis identifier.
Press feed_hold_button to prevent any automatic restart command from the controller.
Walk to servo_cabinet and read_sensor servo_drive_status_led to confirm drive fault state.
Notify maintenance_technician of servo fault with the axis identifier and fault code.
Wait 30 seconds for drive bus capacitors to discharge before touching the cabinet.
Press servo_reset_button on the affected axis drive card.
Read_sensor servo_fault_display to confirm the fault has cleared before releasing feed hold.

sop_examples.title: Axis Hard Limit Overtravel Response
sop_examples.condition: A machine axis has triggered the hard limit switch by traveling beyond the programmed soft limit or physical end-of-travel boundary.
steps: Read_sensor overtravel_alarm_display to identify which axis and direction triggered the hard limit.
Press feed_hold_button immediately to prevent further commanded motion.
Notify CNC_operator of overtravel alarm specifying the faulted axis.
Walk to HMI_panel and press axis_override_enable_button to permit limited manual jog movement.
Press jog_axis_retract_button in the reverse direction to back the axis off the limit switch.
Read_sensor overtravel_alarm_display to confirm the overtravel alarm has cleared.
Notify maintenance_technician to investigate the root cause before resuming automatic operation.

sop_examples.title: Automatic Tool Changer Carousel Jam
sop_examples.condition: The automatic tool changer carousel fails to rotate to the commanded tool pocket position and halts mid-index.
steps: Read_sensor atc_fault_display to capture the ATC error code and the commanded pocket number.
Press estop_button to prevent further motion commands from reaching the ATC mechanism.
Notify maintenance_technician of ATC jam with current carousel position and commanded pocket number.
Walk to atc_access_panel and read_sensor atc_home_sensor to confirm the carousel's actual position.
Wait 15 seconds for spindle to fully decelerate before approaching the ATC zone.
Pick atc_manual_crank_handle and place at atc_access_opening for technician use.
Notify CNC_operator once ATC is cleared to resume tool setup sequence.

sop_examples.title: Chip Conveyor Overload and Jam Response
sop_examples.condition: Chip conveyor motor overcurrent relay trips during a machining cycle, stopping chip removal from the machine enclosure.
steps: Read_sensor chip_conveyor_overload_indicator to confirm the relay has tripped.
Press chip_conveyor_stop_button to fully de-energize the conveyor drive.
Notify CNC_operator to pause machining to prevent chip buildup in the enclosure.
Walk to chip_conveyor_access_door and pick chip_clearing_hook.
Place chip_clearing_hook at jam_location to break up and remove the compacted chip nest.
Press chip_conveyor_reset_button to reset the overload relay.
Press chip_conveyor_start_button and read_sensor chip_conveyor_overload_indicator to confirm normal current draw.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Spindle Bearing Lubrication
sop_examples.condition: Weekly spindle bearing oil lubrication service is due per the preventive maintenance schedule.
steps: Walk to maintenance_supply_cabinet and pick spindle_oil_cartridge.
Press lubrication_pump_button to inject the metered oil dose into the spindle bearings.
Wait 10 seconds for oil to distribute through the bearing races.
Read_sensor spindle_oil_level_sight_glass to confirm oil level is within the normal operating band.
Place empty spindle_oil_cartridge at used_consumable_bin and notify maintenance_technician that service is complete.

sop_examples.title: Linear Guideway Lubrication Replenishment
sop_examples.condition: Bi-weekly linear guideway oil replenishment is due per maintenance schedule, or automatic lube unit low-level indicator is active.
steps: Walk to maintenance_supply_cabinet and pick way_oil_reservoir.
Read_sensor lube_unit_level_gauge to verify the reservoir level before adding oil.
Press lube_unit_fill_button to transfer oil into the automatic lube unit reservoir.
Wait 5 seconds for the transfer to complete.
Read_sensor lube_unit_level_gauge to confirm reservoir is at the full mark, then notify maintenance_technician.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Sump Filter Element Replacement
sop_examples.condition: Monthly coolant filter replacement interval is due, or the filter bypass indicator lamp is illuminated on the coolant system panel.
steps: Press coolant_pump_off_button to de-energize the coolant system.
Wait 15 seconds for residual coolant flow to stop.
Walk to coolant_filter_housing and pick used_coolant_filter.
Pick replacement_coolant_filter and place at coolant_filter_housing to install the new element.
Press coolant_pump_on_button and read_sensor coolant_pressure_gauge to verify pressure is within normal range.
Notify maintenance_technician that filter replacement is complete and log the service date.

sop_examples.title: Spindle Drive Belt Replacement
sop_examples.condition: Quarterly spindle drive belt inspection reveals cracking, glazing, or stretch beyond the wear limit indicator.
steps: Walk to machine_lockout_station and pick lockout_hasp.
Place lockout_hasp at main_power_disconnect and press disconnect_off_button to lock out main power.
Walk to spindle_belt_access_cover and pick belt_cover_bolts.
Place belt_cover_bolts at parts_tray then pick worn_spindle_belt from the spindle pulley.
Place worn_spindle_belt at inspection_bench for condition documentation.
Pick replacement_spindle_belt and place at spindle_pulley to route and tension the new belt.
Notify maintenance_technician that belt installation is complete and machine is ready for lockout removal.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Tank Semi-Annual Drain and Refill
sop_examples.condition: Semi-annual coolant tank drain, flush, and fluid replacement is scheduled on the preventive maintenance calendar.
steps: Press coolant_pump_off_button and wait 30 seconds for fluid to drain back to the sump.
Walk to coolant_drain_valve and press coolant_drain_open_button to begin emptying the tank.
Wait 120 seconds for the tank to fully drain.
Pick coolant_tank_scrub_brush and place at coolant_tank_interior to scrub sludge and tramp oil deposits.
Press coolant_rinse_valve_button to flush the tank interior with clean water.
Pick fresh_coolant_concentrate and place at coolant_fill_port to begin refilling at the correct mix ratio.
Notify maintenance_technician when the tank is refilled and ready to return to service.

sop_examples.title: ATC Cam and Gripper Scheduled Lubrication
sop_examples.condition: Monthly automatic tool changer cam and gripper jaw lubrication is due per the preventive maintenance schedule.
steps: Press atc_index_disable_button to lock the carousel against rotation during the service.
Walk to maintenance_supply_cabinet and pick atc_grease_cartridge.
Press grease_inject_button to deliver the metered grease dose to the cam mechanism.
Walk to atc_gripper_lubrication_point and place atc_grease_cartridge at atc_gripper_lubrication_point to grease the gripper jaws.
Notify maintenance_technician that ATC lubrication is complete and log the service date.

sop_examples.title: Machine Lockout-Tagout Before Maintenance
sop_examples.condition: Planned maintenance activity requires the machine to be fully de-energized and locked out before any personnel enter the work envelope.
steps: Notify CNC_operator to complete the current program cycle and bring the machine to the safe home position.
Press spindle_stop_button then press coolant_pump_off_button to stop all active systems.
Walk to main_power_disconnect and press disconnect_off_button to cut all main power.
Pick lockout_hasp and place at main_power_disconnect.
Pick lockout_padlock and place at lockout_hasp to secure the disconnect in the off position.
Pick warning_tagout_tag and place at main_power_disconnect.
Notify maintenance_technician that LOTO is fully applied and the machine is safe for maintenance entry.

sop_examples.title: Unplanned Emergency Stop Activation Response
sop_examples.condition: An emergency stop button has been activated unexpectedly, halting all machine motion without prior coordination.
steps: Read_sensor estop_indicator_light to confirm E-stop circuit is active.
Notify CNC_operator to clear all personnel from the machine work zone perimeter.
Walk to the machine perimeter and read_sensor axis_position_display to document the axis positions at time of stop.
Read_sensor spindle_rpm_sensor to confirm spindle has reached zero before approaching the enclosure.
Notify maintenance_technician of the unplanned E-stop event with machine state details.
Wait 30 seconds after spindle reads zero RPM before approaching the machine enclosure door.
Press estop_reset_button only after maintenance_technician has investigated and authorized restart.

sop_examples.title: Minor Coolant Spill Containment
sop_examples.condition: A coolant spill of less than 2 liters is present on the floor around the machine, creating a localized slip hazard.
steps: Notify CNC_operator to pause machine operations.
Walk to spill_kit_cabinet and pick absorbent_mat_roll.
Place absorbent_mat_roll at spill_area to contain and absorb the coolant.
Wait 60 seconds for the absorbent material to fully soak up the fluid.
Pick saturated_absorbent_mat and place at coolant_waste_container for disposal.
Read_sensor coolant_level_sensor to check for an ongoing drip or weeping fitting as the source.
Notify maintenance_technician to inspect fittings and drip tray for the leak origin.

sop_examples.title: Major Coolant Spill Emergency Response
sop_examples.condition: A large coolant release of more than 10 liters has occurred from a ruptured hose, failed fitting, or tank breach.
steps: Press estop_button immediately to stop all machine motion and the coolant pump.
Notify shift_supervisor and safety_officer of a major coolant release requiring evacuation of the immediate area.
Press coolant_pump_emergency_off_button to cut coolant supply at the source.
Walk to spill_kit_cabinet and pick large_spill_berm_kit.
Place large_spill_berm_kit at drain_location to block floor drains and prevent fluid from entering the drainage system.
Wait for safety_officer to arrive and authorize personnel to re-enter the spill zone.
Notify maintenance_technician to isolate and repair the ruptured coolant line or fitting.

sop_examples.title: Daily Machine Startup Sequence
sop_examples.condition: Machine is at a cold start state before the first shift and requires full initialization before production.
steps: Walk to main_power_disconnect and press disconnect_on_button to restore main electrical power.
Press control_power_on_button on HMI_panel to initiate CNC controller boot sequence.
Wait 45 seconds for the controller to complete its boot and self-check routine.
Read_sensor controller_status_display to confirm the controller has reached the ready state.
Press coolant_pump_on_button and read_sensor coolant_pressure_gauge to verify coolant system is within normal range.
Press automatic_lube_cycle_button to execute the initial way lubrication cycle before first axis motion.
Notify CNC_operator that the machine has completed startup and is ready for production.

sop_examples.title: End-of-Shift Machine Shutdown Sequence
sop_examples.condition: The last production part of the shift has been completed and the machine must be shut down for end-of-shift.
steps: Notify CNC_operator to confirm all programs have completed and no part is in cycle.
Press spindle_stop_button to ensure the spindle is fully de-energized.
Press coolant_pump_off_button to stop coolant circulation.
Walk to chip_conveyor_panel and press chip_conveyor_off_button to stop the chip conveyor.
Press control_power_off_button on HMI_panel to initiate CNC controller shutdown.
Wait 30 seconds for the controller to complete its shutdown sequence.
Walk to main_power_disconnect and press disconnect_off_button to cut main electrical power.

sop_examples.title: Belt Speed Below Minimum Setpoint
sop_examples.condition: The belt speed sensor reads below the minimum operating threshold (setpoint minus 10%) while the conveyor is commanded to run, triggering a yellow warning but no overload trip.

sop_examples.title: Belt Overspeed Alarm
sop_examples.condition: The belt speed sensor reads above the maximum rated speed ceiling, triggering a red overspeed fault that requires an immediate controlled stop before investigation.

sop_examples.title: Belt Fully Stopped Due to Jam
sop_examples.condition: The belt has come to a complete hard stop and the drive motor has tripped its overload relay due to a material jam or mechanical blockage in the belt path.

sop_examples.title: Photo-Eye Fault During Production
sop_examples.condition: A photo-eye on the infeed or outfeed has tripped unexpectedly during normal production without any actual obstruction present, halting conveyor motion.

sop_examples.title: Belt Mistracking Warning
sop_examples.condition: The belt tracking sensor detects the belt has drifted off-center beyond the warning band but has not yet contacted the conveyor frame, allowing continued operation.

sop_examples.title: Belt Severe Mistracking Emergency
sop_examples.condition: The belt has ridden fully off-track and is in hard contact with the conveyor frame, generating a frame-contact fault that commands an immediate emergency stop.

sop_examples.title: Drive Motor Overtemperature Alarm
sop_examples.condition: The drive motor temperature sensor exceeds the high-temperature alarm setpoint, triggering a thermal overload warning while the belt is still running.

sop_examples.title: Emergency Stop Activation Response
sop_examples.condition: An emergency stop button has been activated on the conveyor, causing an immediate uncontrolled halt; the root cause must be identified and cleared before any reset is permitted.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Belt Tension Measurement
sop_examples.condition: The weekly preventive maintenance interval requires verification that belt tension is within the specified operating range before the production shift begins.

sop_examples.title: Head and Tail Pulley Bearing Lubrication
sop_examples.condition: The monthly lubrication interval for head and tail pulley bearings has elapsed per the preventive maintenance schedule.

sop_examples.title: Drive V-Belt Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The drive V-belt connecting the motor to the head pulley has reached its wear limit or shows visible cracking and glazing, requiring replacement during a scheduled downtime window.

sop_examples.title: Full Conveyor Belt Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The conveyor belt has exceeded its service life or sustained irreparable damage such as exposed cords or a longitudinal tear, requiring complete removal and replacement of the belt.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Photo-Eye Lens Cleaning
sop_examples.condition: The bi-weekly PM schedule requires cleaning of all photo-eye lenses to prevent nuisance trips caused by accumulated metal dust and coolant mist.

sop_examples.title: Drive Motor Ventilation Filter Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The drive motor cooling filter has reached its replacement interval, or a sustained upward trend in motor temperature readings indicates restricted airflow through the filter screen.

sop_examples.title: Periodic Belt Surface Wear Inspection
sop_examples.condition: The monthly inspection interval requires evaluation of the belt surface for cuts, tears, exposed cords, or excessive top-cover wear that threatens structural integrity.

sop_examples.title: Belt Scraper Blade Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The primary belt scraper blade has worn below the minimum contact thickness or is no longer clearing material from the belt surface at the head pulley.

sop_examples.title: Conveyor Lockout Tagout Procedure
sop_examples.condition: Maintenance or repair work requiring physical access to the conveyor mechanism must be preceded by full isolation and locking of all energy sources.

sop_examples.title: Parts Spill on Conveyor Area Response
sop_examples.condition: Automotive components have fallen off the belt or spilled from a container onto the floor or into the conveyor structure, creating a slip hazard and potential jam risk.

sop_examples.title: Fire or Smoke Detected Near Conveyor
sop_examples.condition: Smoke or open flame has been observed near the conveyor drive motor, belt surface, or surrounding structure, requiring immediate emergency shutdown and fire suppression.

sop_examples.title: Standard Shift Startup Sequence
sop_examples.condition: Beginning of shift startup requires the conveyor to be energized and brought to operating speed in the correct sequence with pre-run sensor verification.

sop_examples.title: Standard Shift Shutdown Sequence
sop_examples.condition: End of shift requires the conveyor to be stopped in a controlled ramp-down sequence and confirmed fully stationary before the area is released.

sop_examples.title: Belt Surface Contamination and Cleanliness Inspection
sop_examples.condition: Quality control protocol requires verification that the belt surface is free of oil, grease, metal chips, or other contamination that could transfer onto finished automotive components.

sop_examples.title: Low Coolant Pressure Warning Response
sop_examples.condition: The coolant pressure sensor reads below the 15 PSI minimum warning threshold during steady-state pump operation with no abrupt change in the reading trend.

sop_examples.title: Sudden Coolant Pressure Collapse Emergency
sop_examples.condition: The coolant pressure sensor registers a rapid drop from normal operating range to below 5 PSI within 10 seconds, indicating a catastrophic loss event rather than a gradual decline.

sop_examples.title: High Coolant Pressure Overpressure Response
sop_examples.condition: The coolant pressure sensor reads above the 80 PSI maximum ceiling during normal operation, indicating an overpressure condition requiring immediate relief.

sop_examples.title: Low Coolant Tank Level Refill Warning
sop_examples.condition: The coolant level sensor reads below the 25 percent refill warning mark in the main coolant tank during normal production, with the pump still running and no interlock tripped.

sop_examples.title: Critical Coolant Level Emergency Shutdown
sop_examples.condition: The coolant level sensor reads at or below the 5 percent emergency cutoff mark, triggering the automatic pump interlock and halting production.

sop_examples.title: High Coolant Temperature Warning Response
sop_examples.condition: The coolant temperature sensor reads above the 55 degrees C advisory setpoint but below the 75 degrees C emergency threshold, with the pump still operating normally.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Temperature Emergency Shutdown
sop_examples.condition: The coolant temperature sensor reads above the 75 degrees C emergency threshold, requiring immediate pump shutdown to prevent system damage and thermal runaway.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Pump Motor Electrical Fault Response
sop_examples.condition: The pump motor current sensor triggers an overcurrent or ground fault alarm, illuminating the motor fault indicator on the control panel, unrelated to thermal or mechanical jam conditions.

sop_examples.title: Minor Coolant Leak at Fitting or Hose
sop_examples.condition: A small seep or drip of coolant is detected at a hose fitting or compression joint, producing a slow accumulation of less than one liter per hour with no pressure loss on the system gauge.

sop_examples.title: Major Coolant Line Rupture Emergency Response
sop_examples.condition: A large-volume coolant release is observed from a failed hose or ruptured fitting, producing a continuous high-flow spill exceeding 10 liters per minute and requiring immediate system shutdown.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Filter High Differential Pressure Warning
sop_examples.condition: The filter differential pressure sensor reads above the 25 PSI clogging warning limit, indicating the filter element is partially blocked and will require replacement within the next scheduled maintenance window.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Concentration Below Minimum Specification
sop_examples.condition: The coolant concentration sensor reads below the 5 percent minimum Brix specification, indicating the mixture is too dilute and presents elevated corrosion or microbial risk.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Concentration Above Maximum Specification
sop_examples.condition: The coolant concentration sensor reads above the 10 percent maximum Brix specification, indicating an overly rich mixture likely to cause foaming or residue buildup on machined parts.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Coolant Filter Element Replacement
sop_examples.condition: The filter element has reached its 500-hour scheduled replacement interval, or a differential pressure warning has been planned into the next maintenance window.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Coolant Tank Top-Off
sop_examples.condition: The coolant level sensor reads between 25 and 40 percent of tank capacity during a planned maintenance window, requiring a top-off to restore the operating level without emergency conditions present.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Coolant Pump Bearing Lubrication
sop_examples.condition: The pump bearing lubrication interval of 1000 operating hours has elapsed per the preventive maintenance schedule, with no bearing noise or elevated temperature currently observed.

sop_examples.title: Periodic Coolant Concentration Mixing Adjustment
sop_examples.condition: The coolant concentration sensor reads within one Brix unit of a specification boundary during a routine weekly check, requiring a corrective mixing cycle before the reading goes out of spec.

sop_examples.title: Scheduled Coolant System Flush and Clean
sop_examples.condition: The coolant system has reached its quarterly flush interval, or visible biological growth, dark discoloration, or abnormal odor has been detected in the coolant tank.

sop_examples.title: Coolant System Lockout-Tagout Procedure
sop_examples.condition: Maintenance work requiring physical intervention on the coolant system components is scheduled, necessitating full energy isolation and tagging before any technician begins work.

sop_examples.title: Coolant Spill Floor Cleanup Response
sop_examples.condition: Coolant fluid is found pooled on the floor surface in the machining area creating a slip hazard, with no active high-volume source currently releasing fluid.

sop_examples.title: Coolant System Emergency Stop Activation
sop_examples.condition: A fire alarm, personnel injury, or uncontrollable equipment failure in the machining area requires immediate and complete stop of all coolant system operation.

sop_examples.title: Coolant System Daily Production Startup
sop_examples.condition: The start of a production shift requires the coolant system to be brought from idle to full operating status before machining equipment is released to run.

sop_examples.title: Basin Water Level Below Minimum Setpoint
sop_examples.condition: The basin level sensor reads below the 18-inch minimum setpoint while the recirculating pump is running, risking pump cavitation.

sop_examples.title: Basin Water Level Above Maximum Setpoint
sop_examples.condition: The basin level sensor reads above the 26-inch maximum setpoint, creating imminent overflow risk onto the mechanical room floor.

sop_examples.title: Fan Motor Temperature High Alarm While Running
